transcript:
Meet header:
Date: 2026-06-23
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Lane (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (CTO - Lighthouse), Priya Singh (Product), Daniel Kim (SRE), Aisha Bello (Finance)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be fuzzy):
Sophie opened with value props, Ethan demoed console focusing on Path Insights, per-path cost breakdown and how to map to billing. Customer asked about security and on-prem/private deployment options. Agreement to run a pilot on the chat path.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. I'm Sophie from Redwood, AE on the Lighthouse account. With me is Ethan, our solutions engineer. Quick round of intros?
[00:12] Marco: Yeah hi this is Marco, CTO at Lighthouse. Priya and Daniel are on as well, Aisha from finance will listen in for the cost bits.
[00:20] Ethan: Great, thanks. We'll run through the Console view — focusing on path level insights, cost breakdown, and a short discussion on pilot mechanics. We'll leave time for Q and A.
[00:35] Priya: Sounds good, we care most about the chat and triage flows, those are 70% of calls.
[00:42] Sophie: Got it. Ok Ethan, over to you for a live walk.
[00:47] Ethan: Cool, I'm sharing my screen now. So this is the Console home — note the overall usage lens, but I'm gonna jump to Path Insights. You'll see we surface per-path latency and token usage, and an attribution column to map to cost centers.
[01:10] [screen noise / typing]
[01:18] Ethan: For Lighthouse you'd create a path for each logical flow — chat, triage, summarization, report-gen. Each path gets an ID and we correlate tokens + model inferences. Here you can pivot by model or by time window.
[01:36] Marco: Is that derived by header or do we need to instrument call metadata?
[01:42] Ethan: We can auto-infer by route pattern (we have heuristics), but best practice is to tag requests at the app layer. It's low friction — a single header (x-redwood-path) or route name in the SDK. If you can't change code right away you can use our routing rules to map endpoints.
[02:05] Daniel: If we tag, can Redwood keep PII out of logs? We're under HIPAA-ish constraints.
[02:12] Sophie: Good call — we have privacy-by-default, we filter PII from logs and you can opt to disable payload retention. We'll send the SOC2 & HIPAA note in the security pack.
[02:24] Ethan: On the dashboard, here's per-path tokens consumed and a cost estimate. Note how we break down into prompt tokens, completion tokens, and KV cache hits. KV cache reduces repeated prefix token counts — we show estimated token savings in a column.
[02:48] [00:02-ish laughter]
[02:55] Priya: That KV cache savings number — is it an estimate or real measured?
[03:01] Ethan: It's measured when the cache is enabled. For historical data we run a sim over past traces to estimate potential savings. It's accurate within a band, but we'll label it as estimate in the UI.
[03:20] Marco: Can we get per-customer or per-tenant slices? We need to charge back to our customers.
[03:26] Ethan: Yes, per-path attribution can be combined with tenant metadata. If you send tenant-id as a tag we can break down costs by tenant and export CSV for billing.
[03:38] Daniel: On batching — how does that affect latency especially for chat where we need low tail latency?
[03:45] Ethan: Good question. The Console shows trade-offs: effective throughput improvements from batching vs p95 latency. For low-latency chat we recommend small batch windows and continuous batching tuned to your QPS. We can set per-path batching policies — e.g., chat path gets priority route with 20ms batching window and a dedicated capacity pool if needed.
[04:15] Priya: Dedicated capacity — what's the commitment?
[04:20] Sophie: Dedicated is monthly reserved capacity, configurable GPU pools. For pilot we usually start hosted with capping, then shift to dedicated once volume stabilizes. We'll outline numbers in the pilot doc.
[04:33] Ethan: Back to the Console: here's a per-path cost waterfall — infra, model compute, token charges, and any applied discounts. You can drill into time-of-day, and there's a per-token cost breakout so you can see which prompts are driving majority of spend.
[04:56] [05:00] Aisha: On the discounts — do you have enterprise price tiers? We need to forecast budgets for the next quarter.
[05:07] Sophie: Yes, we have usage tiers and committed spend discounts. I'll include a pricing sketch and a sample projection in the follow up.
[05:15] Marco: How about fallbacks — if a preferred model is unavailable, can we autoswitch to smaller models? We need consistent availability for critical chat.
[05:25] Ethan: Absolutely. Policy-based fallback is part of routing. We show the fallback chain in the route config and you can set SLOs that control when to fallback. The Console visualizes failure modes and automatic rollback counts.
[05:40] Marco: Any observability for hallucinations or quality regressions?
[05:46] Ethan: We wire in prompt-based evals — you can attach test prompts to a path and track quality metrics over time. If a rollout causes a regression the system can alert and auto-roll back.
[05:58] Priya: Nice. Could we run a canary on just 5% of traffic for the chat path?
[06:03] Ethan: Yep, per-path canaries are supported. You can choose traffic slice and metrics for gating.
[06:10] [06:10] Sophie: Ok let's show the actual spend breakdown for a sample customer — this is anonymized, but shows per-path charges. See how chat is 62% of spend even though it's 70% of requests — higher completion tokens per request.
[06:30] Ethan: We also show token distribution heatmaps so you can identify prompts with outlier completion lengths. Those are good candidates for prompt engineering or model choice shift.
[06:44] Marco: On model choice — can Redwood suggest quantized variants or cheaper family models per path?
[06:50] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Optimize suggests model & quantization combos. The Console surfaces recommended alternatives and estimated cost delta and a predicted quality degradation band. It's a suggestion — you can preview outputs before switching.
[07:10] Priya: If we wanted to do that for triage path first, can we get a simulated cost savings?
[07:16] Ethan: We can run a dry-run simulation on your sample traces. That'll be part of the pilot plan.
[07:24] [07:24] Daniel: Network-wise, if we run Private (VPC) do you require egress rules or open ports?
[07:30] Sophie: For Private deployment we provide a customer-managed control plane with explicit ports/policies documented. We'll include the network checklist in the security packet.
[07:42] Marco: How do you handle encryption & keys? Do you support our KMS?
[07:47] Ethan: Yes, we integrate with common KMS providers and HSMs. You can bring your key for at-rest and in-transit encryption. We'll include details in the security doc.
[07:58] [static / partial word drop]
[08:05] Priya: About data retention — can we set retention windows per path? We need 30-day retention for chat logs for debugging and then purge.
[08:13] Ethan: Yep, retention is configurable per-route. You can also disable payload retention entirely and only keep metrics.
[08:21] Sophie: We've got about 35 minutes left — any deep technical items you want Ethan to demo?
[08:28] Marco: Can you show the CSV export and the billing mapping? We want to import into our finance system.
[08:34] Ethan: Sure. Pop open the path -> export. You can choose dimensions: time window, tenant-id, model, prompt/completion tokens. Export formats: CSV or parquet. There's also a webhook push into your BI pipeline.
[08:52] Priya: Parquet would be great.
[08:54] Ethan: We'll include the sample export schema in follow up.
[09:00] [09:00] Daniel: For the pilot scope — how long, and what's success criteria?
[09:05] Sophie: We typically run a 3-week pilot: week 0 ingest sample traffic + instrument tags, week 1 run baseline measurement, week 2 apply optimizations (batching, caching, model changes) and measure delta. Success criteria: 20% cost reduction or p95 latency below X for chat path, and clear billing export into your systems. We'll draft with Ethan.
[09:30] Ethan: I'll put together a lightweight runbook and proposed SLOs.
[09:35] Marco: One more question — have you observed token spikes from multi-turn contexts? Any guardrails?
[09:41] Ethan: We track conversation depth and token growth. The Console can flag sessions crossing thresholds and we can apply server-side truncation or summary-based compaction. We show that as potential quality vs cost trade-off.
[09:58] [10:00] Aisha: From finance perspective — can we get monthly forecasting views with scenario modeling?
[10:05] Sophie: Yes we have a Forecast tab that runs scenarios (growth %, model mix changes) and outputs expected spend. We'll attach a sample forecast sheet.
[10:16] Priya: Ok let's talk timeline — we aim to start pilot next week. Can you be ready?
[10:21] Sophie: Yes we'll aim for week of 6/29. After the call we'll share pilot scope doc, security pack, and a small checklist.
[10:29] Ethan: Quick demo note — the Console sometimes transcribes UI text as 'Consul' in the transcript, ignore that, it's a small ASR hiccup.
[10:36] Marco: Haha noted.
[10:38] [crosstalk]
[10:42] Sophie: Let's do a quick recap and responsibilities. Sophie to send security pack and pricing sketch. Ethan to draft pilot scope and runbook. Marco share sample traffic. Daniel provide VPC details.
[10:57] Priya: Sounds good. Any blockers?
[11:01] Marco: None on our side, Priya will coordinate internal sign-off for data sharing.
[11:07] Sophie: Great. We'll follow up with calendar invite for pilot kickoff.
[11:12] [11:12] End of call.
